name: State of Minnesota
policy_note: This file is a STRUCTURAL research pointer for students, not a source of substantive law. It states only court-structure facts, citation-format templates, and links to official government research sites. It deliberately contains NO substantive statutory rules — student-facing packets are facts-only, and finding and reading the controlling law is the legal-research exercise. Chapter-level 'where to look' locators are navigational aids only. Instructor notes (separate files) may cite specific provisions, verified at publish.

trial_court.name: Minnesota District Court
trial_court.note: Court of general jurisdiction, organized into ten judicial districts by county. Handles civil, criminal, family, juvenile, and probate matters.

highest_court.name: Minnesota Supreme Court
highest_court.note: Court of last resort; also has original/ultimate jurisdiction over attorney discipline and admission.

specialty_divisions.juvenile: Juvenile Division of the District Court
specialty_divisions.family: Family Court Division of the District Court
specialty_divisions.probate: Probate/Mental Health Division of the District Court

regulator.name: Office of Lawyers Professional Responsibility
regulator.head_title: Director of the Office of Lawyers Professional Responsibility
regulator.note: Investigates and prosecutes attorney-misconduct complaints; the Director files a Petition for Disciplinary Action. This is the real-tier analog of the fictional MOLC.

board.name: Lawyers Professional Responsibility Board
board.note: Board of lawyers and public members; district ethics committees screen complaints; a referee (often a retired judge) is appointed to hold the hearing and make findings.

attorney_discipline.process_flow: Complaint -> OLPR investigation -> district ethics committee -> Director's Petition for Disciplinary Action -> referee hearing -> Minnesota Supreme Court
attorney_discipline.caption_style: In re Petition for Disciplinary Action against <Respondent>, a Minnesota Attorney, Registration No. <#>

research_pointers.note: Official government sources only. Use these to locate and read the controlling law yourselves.
navigational_code_areas: Impaired driving (DWI) offenses are collected in Minn. Stat. ch. 169A — a starting point for the m15 research exercise.
Attorney licensing and discipline authority appears around Minn. Stat. ch. 481 and the Rules on Lawyers Professional Responsibility — a starting point for m12.

disclaimer: Structural/navigational reference only, current as of 2026. Verify all law against the official sources above before relying on it; nothing here is legal advice.
